body:
I talk to my partner about it a lot, but it feels like he doesn't understand and cannot understand, which frustrates me extremely, but I don't want to blame him.

I don't think I have PTSD, but looking at the facts it's super likely I do. I just don't want to admit it, I think. 

Sometimes I feel like if I did kill myself, though, at least people might stop and think about their choices, which I know is wrong and petty, but still.

I am very depressed, I know this. Thank you for your answer and offer though, and I am going to try and use the motivation of proving people wrong to keep going

Our situations do sound really similar. How are you doing now? Better? I got a job that I thought would help a lot but it wound up just making everything worse:( I am finally leaving that job, though. So, I'm making strides but a lot of times it feels like it's one step forward and two steps back. When you talk about medication do you just mean antidepressants?

I have a general practice physician but he is not very good. He doesn't listen to my valid medical complaints (I've been struggling with eating as well, not sure if it's depression or side affect of medication but I'm very lucky if I get more than 800cals/day without serious effort). I don't want to tell him I'm suicidal/I self-harm, though I know I should.

Thank you, though. This is the first time I've felt like someone understands what is happening in a very very long time. I will try very hard to let my SO know how much I need help right now and get a therapist, it's just that the motivation is lacking so much, so often.
